messages:
Maria G: Quick sync — we need partner alignment on the stability escrow for the upcoming SDK/ API changes. This is the plan sketch: 1) announce opt-in grace window (30 days), 2) open certification runway (2 weeks), 3) provide a public rollback lane + shim we support for 90 days. Asking partners to confirm timelines and test coverage.
Alex P: +1. Can we call out the exact breaking surface? that'll make partner test plans concrete.
Maria G: Good call. Breaking surface = auth header format and a small payload envelope change (we're removing `request_id` wrapper). Full diff in the doc: https://redwood.internal/partner-escrow/spec-1768 (PTA)
Samir V: For auth header rotation, can we provide a compatibility header that accepts both formats for the grace window? Example:
```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Redwood-Auth-Version: v2
```
Fallback will accept v1 and v2 during the 30d window.
Jen K: We'll publish an SDK shim (npm/pypi) that toggles the header automatically based on config. Will aim for alpha in 4 business days. @Partner Integrations Bot can you create the canary channel and test harness?
Partner Integrations Bot: Created channel #partner-canary-1768019999 and CICD job partner/compat-run-1768019999. Tests: basic auth path, envelope parsing, and telemetry opt-in. Results will post to channel when runs complete. :robot_face:
Connor (HW Partner): From HW side — firmware SDK (edge runtime) depends on the existing envelope. Our release calendar has a hard freeze two weeks from now. We can target the 30d grace, but need the shim ASAP. Can you share the minimal parsing spec we should implement?
Maria G: Minimal parsing spec pasted below. If header present v2 -> new flow. else -> legacy.
```
- If Redwood-Auth-Version == "v2":
  - expect payload top-level fields: input, metadata
- else:
  - expect payload wrapped in {"request_id": {"payload": ...}}
```
Alex P: Also adding a backward-compatibility test cases matrix to the doc. For marketplace/managed partners, we need to communicate SLA expectations during the grace period (latency/regressions). Who owns partner comms?
Jen K: Solutions team will own partner-facing message drafts. I'll loop in marketing for a joint announcement cadence. Suggest: internal partner preview, then public marketplace notice after 7 days.
Samir V: One more ask: telemetry tags to detect legacy/updated clients. We'll add header Redwood-Client-Compat: v1|v2 to help traffic routing and rollback decisions.
Connor (HW Partner): That telemetry header works for us. Also request a binary package of the shim (tarball) for our CI — npm isn't an option in our air-gapped env.
Maria G: We'll produce tarball + signed checksums and place on S3 with short-lived tokens. I'll update the runbook with instructions for retrieving it in air-gapped setups.
Alex P: Risk note: if partners don't upgrade within the window we plan auto-fallback to model-compat variant with degraded features. Documenting exact functional regressions is important.
Maria G: Agreed. I'll add a compatibility matrix (features available on v1 vs v2) and a rollback playbook (how to flip traffic back per partner). Draft will be in the doc by EOD.
Jen K: I'll schedule a 30-min partner sync tomorrow (invite sent). Agenda: timelines, test matrix, shim availability, marketplace announcement timing.
Connor (HW Partner): Thanks — see you tomorrow. We'll run initial firmware tests on the shim as soon as it's available.
Maria G: Thanks all — tagging action items in the doc. Please add any must-have test cases under the "partner-tests" section. :white_check_mark:
